Class Atecc608

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.security.Atecc608
All Implemented Interfaces:
SecretStore
public final class Atecc608 extends Object implements SecretStore
An ATECC608 secure element on an I2C bus, holding named secrets in data slots. Each slot holds a length byte followed by the value, in two 32-byte blocks. The slots are read in clear with plain Read commands: no read key is compiled into the firmware, and any code on the board can read them. Every command frame and response carries a CRC-16, which catches a corrupted transfer but does not authenticate the stored value.

The chip sits at 7-bit address ADDRESS. A value that is unknown, missing, empty, too long for the caller's buffer, or fails a check is reported as missing, and nothing falls back to a plaintext copy. The instance allocates its buffers once, at construction, and read(String, byte[]) allocates nothing.

      public Atecc608(I2c i2c, SecretSlots slots)

    • read

      public int read(String key, byte[] buffer)
      Description copied from interface: SecretStore
      Copies the value of key into buffer and returns its length, or a negative value when the key is unknown, the secret is missing, the chip does not answer or fails its checksum, or the value is longer than buffer. Allocates nothing; buffer is written only on success.
      Specified by:
      read in interface SecretStore

    • clear

      public int clear(String key)
      Stores value[0..length) under key, rewriting both blocks of its slot so no byte of an older, longer value survives. A length of 0 clears the name. Returns length, or a negative value when the name is unknown, the bytes do not fit the slot, the chip does not answer, or it reports an error (for example a locked data zone). A failed write may leave the slot partly rewritten, so the caller should rewrite it.
      Specified by:
      clear in interface SecretStore

    • clearAll

      public int clearAll()
      Description copied from interface: SecretStore
      Empties every name the store knows, which are the names in its table; a slot that the table does not name is not touched. Tries every name even after a failure. Returns 0 when all were cleared, or -1 when any failed.
      Specified by:
      clearAll in interface SecretStore

    • write

      public int write(String key, byte[] value, int length)
      Description copied from interface: SecretStore
      Stores value[0..length) under key, replacing whatever was there, and returns length. A length of 0 clears the name. Returns a negative value when the name is unknown, the bytes do not fit, or the store refuses the write (for example a locked zone or a missing chip). A failed write may leave the name partly rewritten, so the caller should write it again. Writes come from provisioning code, not from programs that only read secrets.
      Specified by:
      write in interface SecretStore
